title: Dependent Care FSA vs. CDCTC Optimizer
description: Compare a Dependent Care FSA (IRC section 129 exclusion) against the Child and Dependent Care Tax Credit (IRC section 21) plus the optimal combination, with FICA savings on the contribution. Three strategy cards, a $250-grid optimum sweep, and a full OCG v0.4 artifact. Refuses malformed inputs with named reasons; money is float USD exactly as the source computes it.

as_of.description: Tax date YYYY-MM-DD. The node reads no clock; its tax year picks the statutory table (2026+ = Pub. L. 119-21 70404/70405).

filing_status.description: Filing status. 'mfj' selects the joint tier-B step; 'mfs' uses the $3,750 cap and carries the 21(e)(2) flag.

agi.description: Household adjusted gross income in USD dollars, non-negative. Drives the section 21(a)(2) applicable percentage.

marginal_rate_pct.description: Caller-supplied federal marginal rate in percent, 0..100. Not computed from tax tables.

state_rate_pct.description: State income tax rate in percent, 0..100.

num_children.description: Number of qualifying individuals, at least 1. Two or more uses the $6,000 expense cap (IRC section 21(c)(2)) instead of $3,000.

childcare_cost.description: Actual annual childcare expenses in USD dollars, non-negative.

fsa_available.description: Is a dependent care FSA available through the employer? When false no sweep runs and the CDCTC-only strategy is the optimum.

fsa_contrib.description: Optional and echoed only, never used: the source page reads this control (page line 359) and the compute never dereferences it, so the optimum is always the $250-grid sweep.

input_schema_provenance: Top-level properties are exactly the policy_parameters members the kernel reads: as_of (validated, and its tax year selects the constant table), filing_status (three-way compare), agi, marginal_rate_pct, state_rate_pct, num_children, childcare_cost, fsa_available (all validated and dereferenced), plus the optional fsa_contrib (echoed only — the source page reads the control and the compute never dereferences it) and the optional ruleset selector. 'required' lists the eight inputs the kernel dereferences unconditionally.
